ordered_diagnoses: Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum

s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive dyspnea on exertion with significant decreases in blood pressure post-exercise
salient_findings: Rapid dyspnea within 45 seconds of exercise initiation
Decreases in systolic and diastolic blood pressure post-exercise
Well-defined mass within the lower SVC with extension to the interatrial septum
key_facts: 66-year-old female with history of epilepsy, thyroid cancer, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and obstructive sleep apnea
Progressively worsening dyspnea on exertion over 9 months
No associated lower extremity edema, orthopnea, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, chest pain, palpitations, dizziness, or lightheadedness
Lifetime nonsmoker
Normal left ventricular ejection fraction of 60% to 65%
Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum present
Normal pulmonary function tests
SVC peak flow velocity: 74 cm/s cephalad to mass, 124 cm/s caudal to mass
Narrowing of the SVC and decreased blood flow through the site of compression

raw.rationale: The presence of a well-defined mass within the lower SVC with extension to the interatrial septum and a lentiform fat signal mass between the lateral wall of the ascending thoracic aorta and medial wall of SVC, as shown on CT and MRI, is most consistent with a cardiac lipoma. The SVC narrowing and decreased blood flow through the site of compression also support this diagnosis, as it would explain the patient's dyspnea on exertion.

rejected.label: Lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum
rejected.why: While lipomatous hypertrophy of the interatrial septum is present, it does not fully explain the patient's symptoms or the imaging findings of a mass in the SVC.

rejected.label: SVC syndrome due to thrombosis
rejected.why: There is no evidence of thrombosis on the imaging studies, and the presence of a fat signal mass is more consistent with a lipoma.

rejected.label: Mediastinal lipomatosis
rejected.why: Mediastinal lipomatosis is a condition characterized by excessive fat deposition in the mediastinum, but it does not typically cause a well-defined mass or SVC narrowing.

rejected.label: Thyroid cancer metastasis
rejected.why: While the patient has a history of thyroid cancer, the imaging characteristics of the mass are more consistent with a benign lipoma than a malignant metastasis.
